self_assessment.spec_coverage: All items from M3.1.5-architect.json r1 implemented. HANDOFF-0 through HANDOFF-17 addressed. Both design reviewer coder notes (stale at1560 test fix; resident.rs line 17 + GpuTimestamp doc comment reword) applied.
known_limitations: AT-1580 (partial cleanup) is a QA diff-read item — no fault-injection seam exists on real GPU hardware, so this remains a manual audit checkpoint rather than an automated test. Every early-return Err in upload_resident calls cleanup_partial_resident or explicit teardown; QA should read each path against the diff.

AT-1574 (prepare_kernel_checked typed skip on capability device) is tested via pure unit tests (AT-1578/AT-1578b) that exercise the preflight logic without GPU. The full integration path (prepare_kernel_checked on a coopmat kernel where the device truly lacks support) is covered in AT-1531 (typed-skip on Lavapipe) which runs under AXC_ENABLE_GPU_TESTS=1.

The bench q4km matvec/matmul resident benches use simplified 64-byte block size which may not match the exact Q4_K_M block layout. The headline resident_timing_kernels bench is primarily for harness validation; accurate Q4_K_M timings will be profiled on NVIDIA by the orchestrator.
deviations: The resident.rs module uses three crate-level #![allow] annotations (clippy::manual_inspect, clippy::drain_collect, clippy::needless_range_loop) because the partial-failure cleanup closures require tracking multiple owned Vecs across error paths — the alternative enumerate/inspect_err patterns would obscure the CORRECTNESS-2 cleanup ordering that QA must audit against AT-1580. All three are documented with why-comments.

AT-1581 label guard is implemented as an inline assert inside the bench iteration closure (bench can only print to stderr; assert guards the label invariant). A separate substring check would require capturing stderr output which Criterion benches do not support.

timing_honesty_verification.GpuTimestamp_doc_reworded: GPU dispatch duration (submit-to-completion timestamp span; excludes host upload/readback; includes dispatch launch + pipeline latency)
timing_honesty_verification.warmup_mandatory_in_dispatch_resident: No — warmup-discard is a CALLER RESPONSIBILITY (the spec says 2 untimed warm-up dispatch_resident calls discarded by benches/tests). dispatch_resident itself measures ONE dispatch per call. The bench helper resident_min_of_n enforces N_WARMUP=2 before the measured loop. AT-1530 also enforces N_WARMUP=2.
timing_honesty_verification.no_competitive_matmul_tflops: resident_timing_kernels prints ns + timing_source, NO TFLOPS/cuBLAS. naive_gemm_harness_validation prints an explicitly labeled TFLOPS with mandatory qualifiers.

correctness_verification.independent_descriptor_set: ResidentBuffers owns its own descriptor_pool+set; dispatch_resident binds resident.descriptor_set NOT handle.inner.descriptor_set. HANDOFF-9 comment present. AT-1570 would fail if this regressed.
correctness_verification.workgroup_guard_in_dispatch_resident: dispatch_resident checks cfg.workgroups against max_compute_work_group_count BEFORE any GPU work. AT-1579 tests this.
correctness_verification.partial_cleanup_in_upload_resident: cleanup_partial_resident called at every early-return Err after the first allocation; transient upload staging freed on its own error paths; ResidentBuffers only constructed when all objects exist. AT-1580 is a QA diff-read checkpoint.
correctness_verification.HN6_query_reset_ordering: cmd_reset_query_pool is the FIRST recorded command in dispatch_resident CB, before any write_timestamp. Only on GpuTimestamp path.
